subject: Workplace Skills
title: Building Coalitions
description: A quick, practical guide to Building Coalitions.

hook.text: She pitched her idea in a large meeting with no prior support. It was shot down. She had allies but didn't mobilize.

buildup.text: Big ideas rarely survive a public pitch without pre-work. In large groups, silence reads as opposition.

discovery.text: Pre-sell your idea individually before the group meeting. Get three supporters who'll speak up. Momentum builds.

twist.text: Don't convince everyone in advance. Three vocal allies in a room of ten tips the social proof in your favor.

climax.text: Before important meetings, have individual conversations with key stakeholders. Address their concerns privately first.

punchline.text: Pre-sell before the meeting. Coalitions win rooms.

quiz.question: Why is pre-selling an idea before a group meeting effective?
options: It eliminates the need for formal presentations
Having vocal allies creates social proof and builds momentum publicly
It prevents anyone from disagreeing during the meeting
